The maximum need not be a clipping point: it can be a saturation point, a limiter threshold, or digital full-scale — headroom-to-full-scale and headroom-to-limiter are ordinary, well-defined uses with no clipping anywhere. Remove clipping and the headroom metric keeps operating. The note's removal test quietly assumes the ceiling must be the clipping point, which is one common definition among several. A margin-to-maximum is a parameter, not a state of the clipping phenomenon. STRIKE.

payload.scope: A normative legal threshold invented in common-law practice to protect the accused, built to persist through statute, constitutional amendment, and the standard jury instructions that recite it verbatim.

payload.body: Beyond-reasonable-doubt is the criminal-law standard of proof requiring the prosecution's evidence to establish every element of the charged offense to such a degree that no reasonable alternative conclusion, consistent with the evidence, remains open to the fact-finder. Parameters: (1) domain — criminal proceedings only (civil matters run on the lower preponderance standard, and some courts recognize an intermediate clear-and-convincing standard); (2) proposition — every element of the offense, including mens rea; (3) bearer — the prosecution alone carries it, and it operationalizes the presumption-of-innocence by fixing the threshold the state must clear; (4) evaluation — the jury or judge decides whether a reasonable doubt exists, and that doubt must arise from the evidence rather than from mere speculation. Mechanism of persistence: it is fixed in constitutional law and statute, recited verbatim in standard jury instructions, and taught as a canonical phrase in legal education, so the exact wording carries standing normative force. [formal: dubium rationabile | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.6]

The pinned sense misidentifies its own mechanism (Law 11d): the note grounds the dependency on 'reducing bit depth by quantizing to fewer discrete levels, which is fundamentally a sampling operation.' payload.body: Audio mixing is a human-made practice of blending multiple recorded sound sources into a coherent whole by adjusting levels, panning, dynamics, equalization, time-based effects, and routing to create a unified listening experience. Parameters: (1) source tracks — the discrete audio recordings to be combined; (2) mix bus architecture — the channel strip, subgroup, and master bus configuration that defines signal flow; (3) processing chain — the per-track and bus processing parameters (gain, pan, EQ, compression, reverb, delay) applied to shape balance and space; (4) reference target — the loudness, tonal balance, and aesthetic goal against which decisions are judged. Mechanism of persistence: the practice persists through studio session templates, DAW automation, engineering education, and industry standards (EBU R128, ITU-R BS.1770) that encode mixing conventions and listening expectations. [formal: mixus | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

payload.body: Insert effect is a human-made audio routing configuration in which a signal passes through an effect unit in series between source and destination, with the effect's output feeding the next stage in the chain. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as a standard wiring convention in analog consoles and as a routing option in digital audio workstations, documented in audio engineering literature and maintained through session templates and hardware design. [formal: effectus insertus | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.name: expander

payload.body: Expander is a human-made audio processing technique that increases the dynamic range of a signal by reducing the amplitude of quieter portions relative to louder portions. Parameters: (1) threshold level below which expansion applies, (2) ratio of output-to-input level change below threshold, (3) attack time for expansion to engage, (4) release time for expansion to disengage. The expander operates by continuously comparing the input signal level to the threshold and applying gain reduction proportional to how far below the threshold the signal falls — the inverse of compression, which attenuates signals above the threshold. Persistence mechanism: embedded in hardware compressors/expanders, software plugin architectures, and studio mixing conventions. [formal: expansio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Crossover is a human-made audio signal processing technique that splits an incoming audio signal into two or more frequency bands, each routed to a different destination such as a speaker driver or processing chain. Persistence mechanism: embedded in active speaker designs, passive speaker crossovers, digital audio workstation routing, and live sound processor configurations. [formal: crux-transversalis | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Removal test fails (Law 8b). The accepted carve of limiting is input-threshold gain reduction: 'reduces gain when an input signal exceeds a set threshold, clamping the output' — that is feedforward detection, no loop required. The accepted carve of feedback demands routing a system's OUTPUT back as INPUT. A feedforward limiter (input detection, or a static clamp function) operates with no feedback at all, so removing feedback does not stop limiting operating. Feedback is one implementation variant (output-detection limiters), not constitutive of limiting — and the note itself hedges 'typically via a feedback loop'. The constitutive mechanism is threshold+gain-reduction, not the loop.

payload.body: Dynamic-range-processing is a human-made family of audio signal-processing techniques that modify the dynamic range of a signal by applying variable gain as a function of level: members attenuate either above a threshold (compression, limiting) or below it (expansion, gating). Parameters: (1) threshold — the level at which processing engages; (2) ratio — output-to-input level change beyond the threshold, finite in compression and effectively infinite in limiting and gating; (3) attack and release times governing engagement and disengagement; (4) side of the envelope (above/below threshold). The family persists as the shared vocabulary and practice of audio engineering: the same threshold/ratio/attack/release parameter set is embedded in hardware processors, plugin architectures, studio mixing conventions, and live-sound processor configurations, so a compressor, limiter, expander, or noise gate is recognized as one of the family by its level-dependent gain law. [formal: tractatio-dynamica | substrate: behavior | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.10]

payload.body: Signal amplification is a human-made signal-processing technique in which an electronic circuit uses external power to produce an output signal whose amplitude — voltage, current, or power — is a scaled version of an input signal, while ideally preserving waveform shape and information content. Parameters: (1) the input signal to be amplified; (2) gain — the ratio of output amplitude to input amplitude, set per stage; (3) the target operating level the output must reach (microphone level, line level, speaker level); (4) fidelity constraints — bandwidth, harmonic distortion, and added-noise limits on the scaled output. It persists as circuit topologies in which active devices (transistors, vacuum tubes) modulate an external power supply in sympathy with the input, as gain and level specifications in datasheets and audio standards, and as the repeated design practice of every preamplifier, power amplifier, and mixing stage. [formal: amplificare | substrate: matter | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.4]

This matches the accepted definition of measuring instrument verbatim in mechanism: transduction of a physical stimulus into a scale reading. It is not an INSTANCE_OF signal-processing (a method class, not a device class) and not of a meter in the rhythmic sense; the nearest kind is measuring instrument. A competent audio engineer calling a DR meter 'a kind of meter' means the instrument sense.

payload.body: Audio bus is a human-made audio routing construct that aggregates multiple audio sources into a single channel for collective processing and mixing. Parameters: (1) bus type — aux send, subgroup, master, or stem; (2) signal routing topology — how sources are summed into the bus; (3) processing chain — effects and dynamics applied to the summed signal; (4) level summing — gain structure and headroom management for the bus. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as a standard wiring convention in analog consoles and as a routing object in digital audio workstations, documented in audio engineering literature and maintained through session templates, hardware design, and professional workflow conventions.

payload.body: Sample-rate is the temporal resolution parameter of digital audio, specifying how many discrete amplitude samples are captured per second when converting analog audio to digital. Parameters: (1) nominal rate — common values at 8000, 11025, 22050, 44100, 48000, 88200, 96000, 176400, 384000 Hz; (2) actual rate — the implemented clock speed, which may drift from nominal. Persistence mechanism: standardized by audio industry bodies (AES, IEC), embedded in hardware specifications (ADCs, DACs, audio interfaces), and enforced by software protocols (S/PDIF, AES3, USB Audio). The definition maps the conceptual boundary: sample-rate is the specification, not the physical clock itself, but the abstract rate that determines maximum reproducible frequency (Nyquist = rate/2) and temporal granularity of the digital representation. payload.body: Signal-chain is a human-made conceptual model in audio engineering that represents an audio signal's route as an ordered sequence of processing stages. Parameters: (1) stage list — an ordered set of processing stages (source, gain stage, filter, effect, converter, output) each with defined inputs and outputs; (2) topology — the routing connecting stage outputs to stage inputs, linear, parallel (send/return), or bus-aggregated; (3) boundary signal state — the form of the audio signal (level, format, channel count, sample rate) as it crosses from one stage to the next; (4) insertion point — the position in the sequence where a stage acts, which determines its effect on the whole path. Persistence mechanism: the model is maintained by audio-engineering practice — routing diagrams and patch-bay wiring, DAW channel and rack routing, console signal-flow teaching, and fault-finding documentation that locates a problem by its position in the chain. The chain is a model of the route, not the hardware: the same physical device sits in many different chains, and the chain persists when its components are replaced, because engineers keep re-describing the route in the same ordered terms. [formal: catena signalum | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.1]

payload.name: sample-and-hold
payload.scope: A human-made technique and circuit for capturing the instantaneous value of a continuous-time signal and maintaining that value for a defined period; built to persist through sampling systems, data-acquisition hardware, and analog-to-digital conversion.

payload.name: sample-and-hold
payload.scope: A human-made technique and circuit for capturing the instantaneous value of a continuous-time signal and maintaining that value for a defined period; built to persist through sampling systems, data-acquisition hardware, and analog-to-digital conversion.

payload.body: sample-and-hold is a human-made technique and circuit that captures the instantaneous value of a continuous-time signal and maintains (holds) that value for a defined period. Parameters: (1) capture mechanism — a switch or transistor that closes briefly to track the input; (2) storage element — a capacitor or equivalent that retains the captured voltage; (3) hold duration — the fixed or variable period during which the value is maintained; (4) droop rate — the voltage change during hold caused by leakage current. Persistence: through implementation in analog-to-digital converters, data-acquisition systems, and pulse-code-modulation encoders, where it bridges continuous-time and discrete-time domains. [formal: <latin> | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: feedback-control is a human-made control architecture in which a system's output is continuously measured, compared to a desired reference value, and the resulting error drives corrective action to reduce the difference. Parameters: (1) forward path — the plant or process being controlled; (2) feedback path — the sensor and signal conditioning that measures the output; (3) controller — the element that computes the error signal and generates the corrective command; (4) feedback sign — negative (stabilizing, error-reducing) or positive (regenerative, error-amplifying). Persistence: through design practice across mechanical, electrical, and software systems, formalized in control theory and embedded in automation, instrumentation, and servo mechanisms. [formal: <latin> | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: An audio interface is a human-made device or software system that connects audio sources (microphones, instruments) to a computer for recording and playback, converting analog signals to digital and digital back to analog. Parameters: (1) analog inputs/outputs — number and type of XLR, TRS, RCA connectors; (2) analog-to-digital/digital-to-analog conversion — sample rate and bit depth; (3) input gain control — preamplification per channel; (4) clocking — internal/external word clock synchronization; (5) computer interface — USB, Thunderbolt, PCIe. Mechanism of persistence: manufactured by electronics firms, sold through pro audio retail, maintained via driver software updates, firmware revisions, and compatibility with DAW software standards (ASIO, Core Audio, WASAPI). [formal: audio-interface | substrate: matter | horizon: years | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Parameters: (1) monitoring chain — source signal, conversion, amplification, transducer; (2) monitoring topology — nearfield monitors, headphones, cue mixes, foldback; (3) calibration — level matching, frequency response correction, room treatment. Mechanism of persistence: persists as standardized hardware (monitor speakers, headphone amps) and software routing in DAWs, documented in audio engineering practice, maintained through manufacturing, session templates, and professional training. payload.reasoning: Sense mismatch + nearer rung (Laws 9a, 11d, 11e). The target's accepted definition carves audio-processing as the MAP OF OPERATIONS performed on signals (amplification, filtering, effects). The source's accepted definition carves signal-chain as a conceptual model of the signal's ROUTE as an ordered sequence of stages — an arrangement, not an operation; the operations happen inside its stages. An ordered arrangement of processing stages is not a kind of the processing itself (9a). And the nearest kind already stands: PIPELINE is ACCEPTED and is carved precisely as 'an ordered sequence of processing stages arranged so each stage's output feeds the next' — that is what a signal chain is. The leap to audio-processing skips the completed rung. The coherent arrow is signal-chain INSTANCE_OF pipeline (or CONTAINS the stages).

Category mismatch under the target's accepted carve (Law 11d, 9a). 'Process' is ACCEPTED as a SEQUENCE OF ORDERED ACTIONS that transforms inputs into outputs through a repeatable, traceable flow — with termination conditions. The source's accepted definition carves feedback-control as a CONTROL ARCHITECTURE: a forward path, a feedback path, a comparator, and a controller in a closed, self-correcting loop. Its defining feature is precisely that it is NOT a linear ordered sequence — the loop is continuous and self-referential, and it has no termination condition. An architecture with a feedback path is not a kind of ordered action sequence (9a: the thing is not an instance of a shape it does not have). The filer's note restates the source's own definition ('output fed back to adjust input') rather than showing it meets the target's parameters. If a 'control' entry stood it would be the nearest kind; process is too far and too differently carved.

Sense mismatch: a parameter is not the act of measuring (Law 11d, 9a). The target's accepted definition carves measurement as THE ACT of comparing a quantity to a standard unit — an event with parameters (quantity, unit, standard of comparison). The source's accepted definition carves sample-rate as a PARAMETER of digital audio: the temporal-resolution value (44100, 48000...) specifying how many samples are captured per second. A number that a system carries is not an act performed on a quantity. The filer's note ('the quantification of how many times per second a signal is sampled') describes what the parameter records, not an act of comparison. Law 9a: a thing is not an instance of its own property. The coherent relation is that sampling DEPENDS_ON a chosen sample-rate, or sample-rate INSTANCE_OF value/property — not the measuring act itself.

No nearer rung stands: there is no 'rate' entry in the live graph, so frequency is the nearest available kind (Law 11e satisfied).

True under the target's accepted carve (Law 11d). Interface is ACCEPTED as 'a conceptual boundary or point of interaction between two systems... that mediates exchange by defining what can pass across the boundary, in which direction, and in what format.' An audio interface is precisely that boundary made into a device or software system: it sits between the analog audio world (microphones, instruments) and the digital computer, and it mediates exchange by converting what crosses — analog-to-digital on the way in, digital-to-analog on the way out — defining format and direction. The filer's pinned sense names this exactly. The naming convention itself ('X-interface' = a kind of interface) testifies to the kind-relation. Nearest kind: 'interface' is exactly the kind; no intermediate rung stands (Law 11e satisfied). Specific→general (Law 9) is clean.
